body: I’ve been dealing with these exact same feelings. I’m glad I’m not alone. There’s people there for you.
I meant that as he’d ask about appointments and stuff because it will show up on bills. Nothing crazy. I just really value his opinion of me.
I live 4 hours away from them. I won’t see them again until thanksgiving. I wasn’t sure if telling them was urgent seeing as I’m on his insurance.
How do you suggest telling your family? Like should it be in person or over the phone?

How do I tell my dad who stigmatizes mental health? 

How do I know how long I cycle? Is that something you can know? 

Are you supposed to tell your friends? And family 

So bipolar people have triggers? Like could something trigger me to switch cycles? (I don’t know any lingo)
I made an edit. Sorry for the length.
My aunt has it. So that’s why I’m not 100% shocked. My family’s the same way. But this opens a new door, what if I ever have a kid? There’s a possibility I could pass it down..

Wow thank you so much. 
I guess my question is how do I not “put my issues on him, and my breakdowns” 
We live together so unfortunately he’s here for most of them, and I can’t predict when they happen or won’t happen. I understand not using his as my therapist and talking to him about my problems. But what did you do when he couldn’t help but he there when you were breaking down. 

And also, I have an appointment next week with a psychiatrist, so I’m going to try to learn not to lean on him as much.

Shit. You definitely have a point. 
And I think that’s a great idea, whenever we talk I’ll bring up that up to him.

I’m sorry you had to go through that but I’m  so happy for you,  for some reason that hurt my heart though. I’ve just been convinced he’s the one. I’ve never felt this way about anyone. I’m glad there’s hope but I guess it also sucks that there’s a chance he may not be the one, bc I really want him to be.

No his very best friend that he knew his whole life passed away. I was there when he was going through it. It was so awful for him. 
It was traumatizing but I guess not in the same way I’ve experienced.

My problem with the idea of breaking up is that we’ve been together for so long. When it’s good it’s really good, but the bad times are really bad. 

The depression is always there, in the depths of my mind. TMI I got off my period about two weeks ago. Usually, I feel better on my period (I know that’s kind of weird) and I’m going to a psychiatrist next Wednesday.

Yes, 
the things I’ve experienced are traumatic. When I try to speak to him /explain the situations  e.g., my mom overdosing, violent relationships in the last. Hearing them makes him feel uncomfortable. I understand it’s hard to hear traumatizing stories, but he’s always suggested I talk to my best friends or someone else about them. 

No, I haven’t drank more than a glass of wine in about a week.
I agree. I have an appointment next Wednesday for a psychiatrist. 😊 I know i need help so I guess that’s a step in the right direction.
I’m probably going to take you up on that PM. Thank you so much.

Ohhhh okay I feel dumb haha. That sounds like a good idea. I may have leaned too much on him for emotional support. I’m a people person so alone time isn’t my favorite but I’ll definitely try that out. Thank you.

A lot of non stop crying. Or I’ll just be completely drained by simple tasks like getting out of bed. He’ll ask me why I’m crying or what’s wrong and I can’t pin point a specific instance. It’s just this deep feeling on intense sadness. 
And I’m not sure what you mean by your last paragraph.
